annualReturn.label: Annual return and financial statements
annualReturn.rule: The annual return must reach the CRO within 56 days of the company's annual return date. Where financial statements are attached, the deadline is the earlier of two dates: the annual return date plus 56 days, or the financial year end plus nine months plus 56 days.

firstReturn.note: A company's first annual return falls due six months after incorporation.

penalty.rule: A late annual return carries a penalty of €100 from the day after the deadline, increasing by €3 for each further day, to a maximum of €1,200 per return. The €20 filing fee is separate.

auditExemption.rule: Under section 22 of the Companies (Corporate Governance, Enforcement and Regulatory Provisions) Act 2024, a company loses the audit exemption if it files late more than once in a five-year period.
auditExemption.supersedes: This replaced the earlier position, under which a single late filing cost the exemption for the following two years.

consequences.title: Late filing penalty
consequences.detail: €100 the day after the deadline, then €3 per day, capped at €1,200 per return.

consequences.title: Loss of audit exemption
consequences.detail: Lost where a company files late more than once in a five-year period.

consequences.title: Prosecution of the company and its directors
consequences.detail: Failure to file is an offence under section 871 of the Companies Act 2014, with a Class A fine of up to €5,000 on summary conviction. The CRO may also impose an on-the-spot fine for persistent late filing.

consequences.title: Involuntary strike-off
consequences.detail: The Registrar may begin strike-off proceedings. Once dissolved, company assets vest in the Minister for Public Expenditure and directors may be personally liable for debts incurred while the company stands dissolved.

rbo.rule: A newly incorporated company has five months from incorporation to file its beneficial ownership details. Any change to the beneficial owners must be filed within 14 days.
rbo.basis: Article 30 of the EU's Fourth Anti-Money Laundering Directive, transposed by the Criminal Justice (Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing) Act 2010, as amended in 2018.

strikeOff.rule: Voluntary strike-off requires all outstanding annual returns to be delivered, assets and liabilities of not more than €150, a letter of no objection from the Revenue Commissioners dated within the previous three months, and a notice of intention advertised in a daily national newspaper within the 30 days before the application.

sizeThresholds.note: Thresholds raised by 25% by the European Union (Adjustments of Size Criteria for Certain Companies and Groups) Regulations 2024, in force 1 July 2024 and applying to financial years commencing on or after 1 January 2024.
sizeThresholds.footnote: A company is classified by size where it meets two of the three criteria. Micro and small companies may qualify for audit exemption.
